history.period: 11th-13th century CE (commonly dated to the 11th century)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Digambar Jain Rekha Deul; keep-or-drop decision needed. An 11th-century (within an 11th–13th c. range) sandstone temple at Banda village (locally Deulghera), Raghunathpur II block, built by the Jain community that flourished in the Rarh/Vajjrabhumi region along Pala-period trade networks; tri-ratha plan, soaring curvilinear shikhara (~72 ft), intricate creeper and chaitya-window carvings, makara-shaped water outlet and pillared mandapa. Rediscovered in 1872 by archaeologist J.D. Beglar overgrown by dense forest; now an ASI-protected monument and the most preserved stone deul in Purulia. Town corrected: CSV 'Purulia' is the district HQ — the temple stands at Banda village, ~35 km from Purulia town.

name: Banda Deul Temple
town_description: Banda (locally called Deulghera) is a small rural village in the Raghunathpur II block of Purulia district, western West Bengal — red-soil farmland dotted with ancient Jain deuls, about 35 km from Purulia town and 12–14 km from Raghunathpur.
